Hi Emily — thanks for the heads up and totally understandable.

Short answer: we can do a hybrid approach that keeps the pilot intact while giving you procurement-friendly accounting options. High-level options below (summary first, details attached):

Option A — Window freeze + date extension (no currency change)
- We freeze usage for up to 21 days; unused daily capacity is appended to the end-date on a 1:1 basis.
- No pricing change; existing SLA applies.
- Clean for auditors since dates change rather than invoicing.

Option B — Escrowed rollover credits (preferred for procurement teams)
- Unused pilot value converted to escrowed credits on RW term sheet; credits can be consumed within 90 days after resume.
- Credits are accounted as a standalone line item (easier for invoice/PO treatment).
- We can offer a small conversion uplift: unused days -> credits at list rate + 10% buffer (to give you extra runway).

Option C — Short freeze + SLA uplift on resumed window (ops assurance)
- For the resumed 30-day window we can commit to a higher availability SLA (95.5% -> 99% regional) and prioritized scheduling during burst windows.
- This is conditional on minor commitment to a short success plan and mutual acceptance of runbook.

Attached is a draft term sheet that shows the escrow flow and sample language we typically use. Priyom (cc) — could you confirm technical scheduling feasibility if they elect the SLA uplift?

If Daniel would prefer a single document to take to procurement, I can produce an amendment + DocuSign link for whichever option you pick.

Cheers,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RW_escrow_term_sheet.pdf (pdf)]

Looping in a quick commercial recommendation so Vanessa can give Emily a concrete ask to take to finance.

Recommended concession (safest for both sides):
- Approve Option B (Escrowed rollover credits) with the following limits: up to 21 days freeze; credits valid for 90 days post-resume; conversion at list + 10% buffer.
- Provide a one-time 15% time-limited discount on overage pricing if they convert to a dedicated pilot within 120 days (this incentivizes conversion to a commit without altering current PO).
- Approve the SLA uplift (Option C) for the resumed 30-day window, but require a short runbook and a single engineer sync pre-resume.

Operational notes: Priyom, confirm that the priority scheduling and elevated SLA are feasible for a single resumed window, and whether we need a short standby on-call.

If anyone needs executive approval, we can escalate but I think this fits within delegated discount authority. Vanessa — I leave the customer-facing wording to you.
